newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Suppliers seen patient on Fokker sale.
newsitem.headline: Suppliers seen patient on Fokker sale.

text.p: The major suppliers to Fokker NV seemed willing to wait a few more days for a possible sale of the bankrupt Dutch aircraft maker to South Korea's Samsung Aerospace, Fokker's administrators said on Friday.
"Without having formally made new agreements, the (court-appointed) administrators have the impression that a few more days of delay should not be insurmountable," they said.
In a statement, they said talks were held on Thursday with Shorts, a Northern Irish unit of Canada's Bombardier, Daimler Benz Aerospace, Airbus GmbH and Rolls Royce, all suppliers to Fokker.
The administrators said they had informed Fokker staff that talks were being held in South Korea with Samsung but added that no information on the contents of the discussions was given.
"We cannot make any statements on the timing at which clarity (about a possible takeover) will arise, nor about the chances of succeeding," they said.
Earlier on Friday, Samsung Aerospace Industries hinted that a deal was within sight.
"The Dutch government is demanding a $500-$600 million long-term investment in Fokker and we are favourably reviewing the proposal," a Samsung spokesman said.
"We are undertaking negotiations with the Dutch government in a very amicable, positive manner but no agreement has been reached yet," the spokesman said.
He denied a domestic newspaper report that Samsung had agreed in principle to take over Fokker for $150 million.
The Dutch government said it had no comment on the Samsung spokesman's remarks.

Fokker was declared bankrupt on March 15 after majority shareholder Daimler Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler Benz AG, cut off financial aid, saying it was no longer able to bear Fokker's huge losses.
